November 1717, a newborn was found on the steps of the church of Saint-Jean-le-Rond, which once stood near here.","source_id":"b3039f38-0329-434b-99db-14baf9e905b5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"He'd grow up to be Jean le Rond d'Alembert, mathematician and philosopher.","source_id":"b3039f38-0329-434b-99db-14baf9e905b5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Ahead of you now is Notre-Dame, the heart of Paris and the symbolic heart of France.","source_id":"d1a26b29-cee0-4fcf-b440-3b9d5f3c5a08","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Look down near the west door and you'll find a small bronze star set in the pavement, called kilometre zero — the point from which every main-road distance in France is measured.","source_id":"d1a26b29-cee0-4fcf-b440-3b9d5f3c5a08","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"The wide, windswept square you're crossing is the Parvis — the word comes from paradise — laid out by Haussmann in the 1860s, and the white paving blocks set into it trace the outlines of the cramped medieval streets and houses that once crowded this spot.","source_id":"d1a26b29-cee0-4fcf-b440-3b9d5f3c5a08","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Now the facade.","source_id":"8094c405-a3ea-47cb-91cb-4e791f7f503a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"It's the cathedral's most impressive face — the Romanesque still shows in that solid H-shape, but what you feel is lightness and grace, thanks to the filigree of the central rose window and the gallery above it.","source_id":"8094c405-a3ea-47cb-91cb-4e791f7f503a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Beneath that rose window runs a row of 27 huge figures, the biblical kings who were Christ's ancestors.","source_id":"37e95b17-1dfc-454a-9dbd-0fa8c1d16f5a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Every one is a copy — during the Revolution a mob mistook them for French kings and tore the originals down.","source_id":"37e95b17-1dfc-454a-9dbd-0fa8c1d16f5a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Above the central door, the carving to catch is the Day of Judgement, where in the lower frieze the dead heave themselves out of their graves while Christ presides above, sending the souls on his right to heaven and those on his left to hell.","source_id":"cf823873-9a35-44cf-97f5-83b15ec7c674","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Look at the arch — angels peer out all around it, alert and mischievous, said to be modelled on the cathedral's choirboys of the day.","source_id":"cf823873-9a35-44cf-97f5-83b15ec7c674","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"The side doors tell gentler stories: the left portal shows Mary crowned by Christ with her life below, while the right shows the Virgin enthroned, and beneath her, scenes from the life of her mother St Anne and from the life of Christ.","source_id":"ab3aae94-a724-48d2-8a36-573e734d618f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"The carvers packed them with visual devices and symbols meant to say more than the bare story — in the nativity, the infant Christ lies above Mary to mark his higher status, and rests on an altar rather than a crib, a sign of the sacrifice to come.","source_id":"ab3aae94-a724-48d2-8a36-573e734d618f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Step through the door and you're standing right under the bell tower.","source_id":"102ff4b1-b136-4ab6-82f5-717efce836a9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Look up at the vault and you'll spot the trapdoor the bells were once hoisted through, and the two pillars carrying all that weight are massive.","source_id":"102ff4b1-b136-4ab6-82f5-717efce836a9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Inside, the contrast hits you at once — the nave sits in shadow while light pours onto the first great clustered pillars of the choir.","source_id":"69820c6f-0219-4ada-90fe-781b2a0b5026","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"That light comes from the transept end walls, nearly two-thirds glass, holding two magnificent rose windows that glow imperial purple; the vaulting and the shafts soaring to the springs of the vaults are pure Gothic, while the stout round pillars and the four-square heft are the older Romanesque still holding on.","source_id":"69820c6f-0219-4ada-90fe-781b2a0b5026","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"At the rear, to the right, is the Treasury, holding what's purported to be the Crown of Thorns along with ornate nineteenth-century monstrances and chalices, which may or may not be your thing.","source_id":"06996e8c-2961-42c2-b7da-83f07a086541","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5,"also_cites":["69820c6f-0219-4ada-90fe-781b2a0b5026"]},{"text":"And right at the back, in a side chapel, a set of models shows how the medieval builders actually put this place up.","source_id":"06996e8c-2961-42c2-b7da-83f07a086541","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"If you climb the towers — the entrance is round the side — you'll come face to face with Viollet-le-Duc's gargoyles and angels, and with the great thirteen-ton Emmanuel Bell in the south tower.","source_id":"4b00638a-c069-4145-879c-b7fc3904334d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"One of the largest and oldest bells in Europe, Emmanuel was forged in 1685 and spared during the Revolution of 1789 — unlike Marie, the north tower's bell, which was destroyed and melted down.","source_id":"4b00638a-c069-4145-879c-b7fc3904334d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"It only rings for Christmas, for great occasions, and in times of mourning, like the day after 9/11.","source_id":"4b00638a-c069-4145-879c-b7fc3904334d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"The other nine bells had drifted badly out of tune, so they were all replaced in 2013.","source_id":"4b00638a-c069-4145-879c-b7fc3904334d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5}]}
